issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, slipping, flaring revs between gears, a gearbox fault message, or the car going into a limp mode that holds one gear.
issues.why: The five-speed automatic in the X-Type is its most reported weak point. On early 2002 cars Jaguar found the reverse clutch piston inside the gearbox was not durable enough, and failures on later years are common past about 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the codes read. If it is slipping, avoid hard driving and get a transmission specialist's opinion; a rebuilt or used unit is usually the fix.

issues.t: Transfer case leaking oil or failing
issues.sym: Oil drips or a burning-oil smell near the front of the car, a clunk or whine from the drivetrain, and in bad cases a loss of drive to the wheels.
issues.why: Every US X-Type has all-wheel drive with a small sealed transfer case next to the transmission. Its output seals leak, and because it holds little oil it can run dry and wear out without anyone noticing.
issues.next: Have the transfer case seals checked for leaks at each oil change. Replacing a leaking seal early can prevent replacing the whole unit after it runs dry.

issues.t: Gear selector fault and limp-home mode
issues.sym: The car won't select the gear shown on the J-gate shifter, a transmission warning comes on, and the car stays stuck in one gear.
issues.why: Jaguar issued a bulletin for 2002-2003 automatics where the J-gate selector assembly lost its position setting, which confused the transmission computer.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. A dealer or specialist can reset or adjust the J-gate assembly before anything bigger is replaced.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from expansion tank or thermostat housing
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, a sweet smell, puddles under the engine, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The plastic coolant expansion tank, its bleed tube, the thermostat and the thermostat housing are among the most replaced parts on the X-Type. Cracks and failed seals let coolant escape.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have a pressure test done to find the leak. Don't keep driving if the gauge rises, because overheating can damage the engine.

issues.t: Coolant hose slipping off at oil cooler
issues.sym: Sudden coolant loss and a low coolant light, sometimes followed by overheating.
issues.why: On some 2002-2003 cars the spring clamp on the oil cooler coolant hose could creep along the hose until the joint let go. Jaguar's fix was to reposition it and add a screw clamp.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check that this hose joint has the extra clamp. If coolant is pouring out, stop and have the car towed.

issues.t: Hissing and hesitation from intake vacuum leak
issues.sym: A hissing sound from the engine bay, rough idle, hesitation, and a check engine light for a lean mixture.
issues.why: The O-ring on the intake manifold tuning valve can leak, and intake manifold gaskets are a commonly replaced part. Either lets unmetered air into the engine.
issues.next: Have a smoke test done to find the leak. The O-ring can often be replaced on its own for little money.

issues.t: Crankcase breather valve wear causing smoke and oil use
issues.sym: Rough running, misfires, extra exhaust smoke, high oil consumption and a check engine light.
issues.why: Jaguar found the crankcase breather (PCV) valve on 2002 cars wore early because its internal spring vibrated. A redesigned valve was released.
issues.next: Have the PCV valve replaced with the updated part and check the oil level often until it's done.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, loss of power and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: The V6 uses one coil per cylinder, and coil packs are among the most replaced parts on the X-Type. Coils on the rear cylinder bank are harder to reach.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find which cylinder is affected. Replace the failed coil, and consider spark plugs at the same time if they are due.

issues.t: Engine stops and won't restart from corroded fuel pump wiring
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or will crank but not start.
issues.why: On some 2004 cars water got into the fuel pump connector on top of the tank and corroded the wiring, cutting power to the pump.
issues.next: If the engine dies, get to a safe place and have it towed. Ask a shop to inspect the fuel pump connector and harness for corrosion.

issues.t: Worn control arms and bushings
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a moaning noise when reversing, wandering on the highway, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Control arms and their rubber bushings are the most replaced suspension parts on the X-Type, and the rear knuckle bushings are known to wear and groan.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected on a lift. Replace worn arms or bushings and get an alignment afterward to protect your tires.

issues.t: Front knocking from sway bar links
issues.sym: A knock or rattle from the front end over small bumps and rough pavement.
issues.why: The bushings in the front stabilizer (sway) bar links wear out.
issues.next: Have the links checked. They are quick to replace.

issues.t: Rust on rocker panels and jacking points
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or holes along the rocker panels under the doors, rusted jacking points, or rust near the rear license plate.
issues.why: Owners report the rockers trap water, and body rust is a commonly reported X-Type problem. Trim near the license plate can also rub through the paint.
issues.next: Inspect the rockers and jacking points before buying or before winter. Treat surface rust early; structural rust needs a body shop.

issues.t: Rear turn signals stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The rear turn signals don't flash even though the dashboard arrow still blinks, so other drivers get no warning.
issues.why: A power circuit in a General Electric module could fail. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 03V011) to replace the module.
issues.next: Have a helper check your rear signals and ask a Jaguar dealer whether the recall was done on your VIN.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold on manual cars (recall)
issues.sym: On a manual-transmission car left in neutral, the car can roll even with the hand brake pulled up.
issues.why: The self-adjusting hand brake lever could malfunction and travel too far. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 04V487) and fitted a manually adjusted lever.
issues.next: Park in gear on hills and check with a dealer that the recall has been completed.

issues.t: Manual gearbox hard to shift or clutch pedal sticking
issues.sym: First or reverse is hard to select when the car is cold, or the clutch pedal stays down after you press it.
issues.why: Jaguar bulletins describe the clutch disc sticking on the gearbox input shaft splines and a weak clutch pedal return on early manual cars.
issues.next: A shop can clean and grease the splines or fit the extra pedal spring Jaguar released. Don't keep forcing gears.

issues.t: Weak air conditioning
issues.sym: The A/C blows cool but not cold, especially in hot weather or at idle.
issues.why: Jaguar found the control valve inside the A/C compressor could degrade on 2002-2008 cars and released a modified valve spring.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and refrigerant charge checked. Ask about the control valve fix before replacing the whole compressor.

issues.t: Power steering squeal or leak
issues.sym: A squeal or squeak when turning the wheel, or power steering fluid leaking from the rack.
issues.why: A seal inside the steering rack can make noise, and Jaguar issued a fluid additive fix. Owners also report racks that leak.
issues.next: Check the fluid level. A shop can try the additive procedure; a leaking rack needs to be resealed or replaced.

issues.t: Exterior door handle stiff or not working
issues.sym: A front door handle feels stiff or does nothing, so the door won't open from outside.
issues.why: The link rod between the handle and the latch can bend. Jaguar released a new rod.
issues.next: Have the door panel removed and the link rod or latch checked. It is usually a small part.

issues.t: Hard brake pedal from failing booster vacuum hose
issues.sym: The brake pedal gradually feels harder and the car needs more effort to stop, especially in hot weather.
issues.why: The check valve in the brake booster vacuum hose can deteriorate in heat, lowering power assist. Jaguar's fix was a new hose.
issues.next: Have the brake booster and vacuum hose tested soon. Reduced assist makes emergency stops longer.

issues.t: Rear brake squeal or burning smell
issues.sym: Squealing or moaning from the rear brakes, or a hot brake smell after driving.
issues.why: On early cars the rear pads could stick in the caliper brackets. The fix is new pads with cleaned and greased brackets.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected. Sticking pads wear quickly and can overheat the rotors.

issues.t: Water in passenger footwell
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front passenger side, a musty smell, or fogging windows.
issues.why: Water could get in around the pollen (cabin air) filter area. Jaguar added a water shield.
issues.next: Check that the cowl drains are clear and the shield is fitted. Dry the carpet fully to prevent mold and wiring damage.

issues.t: Condensation inside headlights
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlight lens.
issues.why: The low-beam cap at the back of the headlight did not seal well. Jaguar released a revised cap.
issues.next: Have the headlight caps checked and replaced. Water left inside can corrode the bulb sockets.

issues.t: Vibration from rear driveshaft
issues.sym: A vibration through the floor that grows with speed.
issues.why: Jaguar traced this to rear differential flange misalignment, flange bolts not tightened correctly, or a faulty driveshaft.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft and flange bolts checked. A shop can correct the alignment or replace the shaft.

issues.t: Airbag warning light on
issues.sym: The airbag light stays on or comes and goes.
issues.why: Owners report airbag light faults on these cars, often traced to the seat occupant sensor or wiring.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. While the light is on, the airbags may not work in a crash.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: A battery or charging warning light, dimming lights, or a dead battery.
issues.why: The alternator is one of the more commonly replaced electrical parts on the X-Type.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery. A weak alternator will drain a new battery too.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor
issues.sym: A check engine light, sometimes with slightly worse fuel economy.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors are a commonly replaced part on aging X-Types.
issues.next: Have the code read. Confirm the sensor is faulty and not reacting to a vacuum leak before replacing it.

issues.t: Key fob won't lock the car
issues.sym: The remote won't lock the doors, even with a fresh fob battery.
issues.why: The flap inside the ignition lock could fail to close, so the car thought the key was still in. Jaguar's fix was a new ignition lock cylinder.
issues.next: Try locking with the key in the door. A dealer or locksmith can check the ignition cylinder.
